issue: Does a conviction under Va. Code § 18.2-53.1 for using or displaying a firearm while committing Virginia robbery qualify as a crime of violence under the Guidelines elements clause, U.S.S.G. § 4B1.2(a)(1)?

sides.position: Use or display of a firearm while committing Virginia robbery is a crime of violence under the elements clause (and the enumerated offense clause), because the offense requires using a firearm while overcoming the victim by violence or intimidation.
cases: United States v. Mao, No. 24-2107, 2026 WL 1162679 (1st Cir. Apr. 29, 2026)

sides.position: Neither Virginia robbery nor Va. Code § 18.2-53.1, alone or in combination, has as an element the use, attempted use, or threatened use of physical force against the person of another, so the elements clause is not satisfied.
cases: United States v. Scott, No. 25-4048 (4th Cir. 2026)

this_court: Neither Virginia robbery nor Virginia Code § 18.2-53.1, alone or in combination, satisfies the elements clause; the district court erred in holding otherwise, and the court respectfully disagrees with Mao.
quote: But having carefully reviewed the reasons the First Circuit gave for reaching its conclusion about the elements clause, we respectfully disagree.
cite: United States v. Raquan Scott, No. 25-4048 (4th Cir. 2026)
